fault: The one failing trial of twenty is the only trial whose DDS transport failed. Nine Nav2 nodes each failed to open the same shared-memory port, fastrtps_port18186, so the participants could not discover each other; the reconfiguration request never reached the executor, every transition attempt returned outcome 0, and the planner exhausted its replanning limit. mission_batch scored that controller_failure, which is a robot outcome, on a run where the robot reached its site inside tolerance and never moved a pod.

fix.classification: mission_batch.transport_initialization_failures scans the launch log the runner already captures; an unfinished trial whose participants could not open a port records infrastructure_failure, which retryable_infrastructure_failure already retries while the launch process is alive. Verified against the real campaign: it flags 1 of 20 trials, with the correct port, and none of the 19 healthy ones.
fix.not_retroactive: The r17 record is immutable and its digest is committed, so it is not rewritten. The campaign stands as collected, with the misclassification recorded here and in docs/current_status.md.
fix.prevention: Per-trial teardown now clears Fast-DDS segments that no live process holds open, read from /proc/*/fd rather than by matching process names. Deleting segments blindly is the opposite fault and has already happened here, so a segment nobody has open cannot by construction be underneath a live participant.

interpretation: Not exhaustion and not the robot. /dev/shm is 16 GB and was not full, the robot drove to its site and stopped there within both tolerances with 0.237 m of clearance and 6.6e-05 m of localization error, and nothing mechanical was marginal. A single port file was left in a state the next stack could not open, which is the stale-segment failure family already on record here, and the near-constant 25.3 s replanning cycle is a timeout rather than a physical event. This is the same defect class as the wall watchdog fixed at 0e71dd3: infrastructure recorded as a robot result.
not_yet_root_caused: Why fastrtps_port18186 specifically was left unopenable after 17 clean trials is not established. The campaign cleared /dev/shm once before starting with zero participants alive, so the poisoned segment was produced during the run, by a teardown that killed a participant before it released its port. The per-trial clearing removes the inherited state regardless of which teardown produced it, and the classification means a recurrence costs a retry rather than a gate.

raw_evidence.note: results/ is gitignored; under ADR 0005 the campaign itself is retained at studies/gate0/records/roundtrip_20_watchdogfix_raw.tar.xz and verified against its audit, so this trial's record survives.

status: DIAGNOSED AND FIXED; the gate is owed a fresh 20 at the fix commit.
